title: 20th Sitting of third session of 2025
presiding: Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Speaker); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim took the chair near the end of this part (per the minutes header)
summary: The 20th sitting of the third session of 2025 opened on 17 November 2025 at 09:01 with the usual prayer, attendance and agenda announcements, and the day's work was the general debate on the government's proposed 2026 state budget (about MVR 64.2 billion). Thirteen members spoke in this part: ruling-party (PNC) members mostly backed the budget, pointing to debt repayment, island projects and spending on health, education and housing, while MDP members called it short on detail and said debt and spending were growing. A recess ran from 10:27 to 11:01, and the debate was still open when this part ends, with no votes taken. The text has dropped marks and jumbled digits, so the attendance figures are read as printed. This part continues the general debate on the 2026 state budget. It opens in the middle of a speech by a member whose header is in part 1, then four members take the floor: the Addu Meedhoo member questions debt-heavy spending, while the Vilingili, North Kulhudhuffushi and North Henveyru members back the budget, citing economic indicators and projects for their areas. The sitting paused for noon prayer from 11:55 to 13:00; the chair then named 18 November as the last day of the budget debate and closed the sitting. No vote is recorded in this part, and the text is badly garbled in places.

items.title: Debate on the proposed 2026 state budget
items.outcome: general debate under way; 13 members spoke in this part and it continues; no vote yet

items.title: Debate on the state budget proposed for 2026
items.outcome: debated; chair set 18 Nov 2025 as the final day of debate

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the budget takes world economic conditions into account and that earlier governments left the large debts now being repaid.
Spoke for the ruling party's parliamentary group, backed the budget and criticised the MDP's record, including unpaid bills.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abdul Rahman
positions: Set out the budget's headline numbers: about MVR 64.2 billion total and about MVR 8.3 billion for public sector investment projects.
Said spending on education and health is raised and noted the Hinnavaru hospital works moving ahead.

speakers.name: Azim Abdul Azeez
positions: Backed the budget, saying projected tax revenue, GST and TGST growth show the economy is recovering.
Answered opposition complaints that projects are not named, saying the Public Finance Act does not require listing specific projects.
Said his constituency was overlooked before and expects its airport and hospital projects to go ahead.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Backed the budget and listed projects under way in his islands, including health centres, police stations, harbours and sports grounds.
Said young people, about 60% of the population, get a large place in the budget.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rasheed
positions: Backed the budget and said the President's island visits show the government acts on what residents ask for.
Raised island harbour, school and sports-ground needs in his constituency and asked that they be built.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Said the budget has no clear plan, detail or accountability and that borrowing and recurrent spending are rising.
Said housing-unit promises have not been delivered and raised the lack of an ambulance and other needs in Maradhoo.

speakers.name: Yoosuf Nasheed
positions: Said most of his constituency's requests, such as harbour, school and engine works, appear in the budget.
Raised land erosion and harbour space as continuing problems.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Abdul Rahman
positions: Fully backed the budget and said it puts large sums into repaying debt left by earlier governments.
Said projects delayed under the previous government are now moving in his constituency, including airport and water works.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Said the budget is not a vision budget, lacks detail and that debt keeps growing, with the public left to repay it.
Criticised subsidies, political appointments and the government's record on institutions' independence, tourism and fisheries.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Backed the budget, noting large debt repayment, funds for judicial independence and bigger grants to island councils.
Said subsidies should be targeted and that former presidents' benefits need review; listed Manadhoo and Maafaru projects.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said the budget gives priority to repaying debt, including keeping the deficit and debt ratios within targets.
Raised water, hospital, school and sports-complex projects for Fuvahmulah and said they are moving ahead.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Backed the budget and said it aims to cut the deficit to 5% of GDP by 2028 and fix earlier fiscal mistakes.
Raised the harbour space problem and land shortage for housing in his constituency's islands.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Backed the budget and said debt repayment is a main goal that the public asked for.
Said projects can only go ahead once the budget passes and criticised opposition claims about the previous government.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Backed the budget and said it supports the President's housing promises for Malé residents.
Said plots handed out earlier will be developed with the budget's funding.

speakers.name: Abdul Rahman
positions: Said much of the 2026 budget goes to debt and interest, and raised concerns about prices, the rufiyaa and the cost of living.
Raised concerns about project spending and loans, including Rasmale, housing units and projects in Addu.
Pointed to the budget's reliance on tourism and urged investing in fisheries, farming and technology.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Congratulated the government on its second anniversary and described budget projects for Kulhudhuffushi, including a duty-free port, hospital building and airport work.
Said health allocations should follow where patients seek care, and asked the committee stage to review the budgets of some institutions.
Noted housing units planned for Kulhudhuffushi and said the budget gives hope to the island.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Backed the budget, saying reserves and the sovereign fund have grown since the government took over, contrary to opposition warnings.
Cited Malé housing plans, including Rasmale, a housing loan scheme and land plots, as promises being delivered.
Cited drug-law reforms, the vape ban and the generational tobacco ban as measures to protect young people.

decisions: The Speaker opened the sitting at 09:01 with the prayer and announced the day's agenda.
The general debate on the 2026 state budget was opened under Rule 235 of the Majlis rules, with members called in turn.
The sitting recessed from 10:27 to 11:01 and the Speaker then resumed the debate.
Near the end of this part Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim took the chair while the Hinnavaru member was speaking.
The chair named 18 November 2025 as the final day of the 2026 budget debate.
The sitting paused from 11:55 to 13:00 for noon prayer, then ran to about 13:30.
The next sitting was set for 18 November 2025 at 9:00 am.
